title: Microsoft Teams: external bot detection and activity reports in the Teams admin center
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap targets and existing bot-policy controls are supported. It distinguishes the planned report from today's controls, identifies the unpublished report details, and accurately notes Microsoft's differing command-value and report-role wording.

claims.claim: The existing bot setting is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting join & lobby > Manage external bots and their access to meetings.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Meetings > Meeting policies. Select the policy you want to modify, or create a new policy. Under Meeting join & lobby, find Manage external bots and their access to meetings.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalBotAccessMode RequireApprovalWhenDetected configures detected bots to require approval.
claims.quote: RequireApprovalWhenDetected: When detected, bots will be enforced to the meeting lobby, regardless of the lobby setting of the meeting. They will require approval before getting access to the meetings. This is the default value.

claims.claim: No admin center report control or API for external bot detection and meeting access reporting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams external bot activity report; external bot report Graph API detections. Read manage-external-bots, reporting reference and Security detections report. Results documented external domain reports and reportSyntheticMedia, not this report or its API.

claims.claim: The existing bot control is a meeting policy applied at user or group level.

claims.claim: The bot setting applies to meetings hosted by users assigned the policy.
claims.quote: The setting applies to meetings hosted by users assigned the meeting policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Teams already documents bot detection and a meeting policy that governs bot handling, distinct from the planned report.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams provides admins with controls to detect and manage external bots when they attempt to join meetings hosted in their organization.

claims.claim: Teams identifies external AI bots using signals collected during the meeting join process.
claims.quote: Teams uses built-in detection mechanisms to identify external AI bots based on signals collected during the meeting join process.

claims.claim: The bot policy has three options: do not detect, require approval when detected, and block detected bots.
claims.quote: Do not detect bots | AllowBots; When detected, require approval before joining (default) | RequireApprovalWhenDetected; Block all detected bots | BlockDetectedBots

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; rationale: risk

claims.quote: | Default value: | RequireApprovalWhenDetected |

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Do not detect bots means bots are neither detected nor marked in the lobby or meeting.
claims.quote: Bots aren't detected or marked in the lobby or in the meeting. They appear as any other external participant in the meetings and follow the meeting's existing access and lobby settings.

claims.claim: Block all detected bots prevents detected bots joining or being admitted by organisers or other participants.
claims.quote: Detected external bots are automatically blocked from joining meetings. They can't be admitted by meeting organizers or other participants.

claims.claim: Block all detected bots does not guarantee every external bot will be blocked.
claims.quote: The Block all detected bots option applies to bots identified by Teams detection mechanisms. It does not guarantee that all external bots will be blocked.

claims.claim: A human incorrectly identified as a bot may be prevented from joining under the blocking option.
claims.quote: Participants incorrectly identified as bots may be prevented from joining the meeting.

claims.claim: Where supported, eligible blocked participants can use email verification recovery.
claims.quote: Where supported, eligible participants can use the email verification recovery experience to verify their identity and attempt to join.

claims.claim: Under the approval option, organisers can admit a participant incorrectly identified as a bot.
claims.quote: Require approval before joining: Organizers can admit the participant from the lobby

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Organisers can use This is not a bot to correct the participant's representation in that meeting.

claims.claim: Get-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" | Select-Object Identity, ExternalBotAccessMode reads the configured bot policy.
claims.quote: To view the configured policy setting: Get-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" | Select-Object Identity, ExternalBotAccessMode

claims.claim: Microsoft's best practices suggest testing the blocking policy with a selected group before applying it organization-wide.
claims.quote: Consider testing the blocking policy with a selected group of users before applying it organization-wide.

claims.claim: Analytics & reports is the Teams admin center navigation area in which to look for reports.
claims.quote: Go to the Microsoft Teams admin center, in the left navigation, select Analytics & reports, and then under View Reports, choose the report you want to run.

claims.claim: The bot management page's prose names Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy but its configuration examples print Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy.
claims.quote: You can use the Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy PowerShell cmdlet to manage this policy option. ... Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -ExternalBotAccessMode RequireApprovalWhenDetected

claims.claim: The bot management page lists AllowBots as its disabling-detection value, alongside RequireApprovalWhenDetected and BlockDetectedBots.
claims.quote: Do not detect bots | AllowBots; When detected, require approval before joining (default) | RequireApprovalWhenDetected; Block all detected bots | BlockDetectedBots

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference instead lists AllowAllBots to disable detection, differing from the bot management page's AllowBots.
claims.quote: AllowAllBots: Don't detect bots; Bots will appear the same as other participants. Standard lobby policies will apply to them. They may get mistakenly admitted to meetings.
